product.name: GPT Repo MCP
product.purpose: Help a solo developer use ChatGPT as a product-aware senior developer, reviewer, and workflow coordinator in trusted local repositories while preserving strong server-side safety, evidence, recovery, and local control.

primary_users.role: Solo developer or small-team technical owner
primary_users.technical_level: Technical, but time-constrained and unable to continuously supervise every agent step
primary_users.work_context: Uses ChatGPT and implementation agents across multiple local repositories and needs fast, trustworthy progress without repeatedly reconstructing project context.

primary_users.role: Developer operating ChatGPT, Codex, or another implementation agent against a trusted local repository
primary_users.technical_level: Comfortable with code and Git, but expects the tooling to preserve product intent and prevent unsafe or incomplete repository operations
primary_users.work_context: Delegates planning, implementation, review, validation, recovery, and local ship work through named MCP tools.

jobs_to_be_done.statement: Understand a repository, its product intent, architecture, current state, and relevant constraints without reading everything manually.
Delegate coherent implementation work to an agent without converting the product goal into a brittle file-by-file script.
Review actual code, Git state, validation evidence, and product outcome rather than trusting an agent summary.
Validate, recover, stage, and create local commits through bounded server-side workflows without arbitrary shell access.
Continue work across sessions and agents without losing decisions, product direction, or current implementation state.

must_reduce: Repeatedly explaining the same repository and product context
Babysitting implementation agents through every internal step
Prompt micromanagement and closed-world file-by-file delegation
Risky manual repository operations that lack review or recovery evidence
Context loss between ChatGPT sessions, Codex runs, reviews, and commits
Technically correct changes that move a product away from its intended user
must_not_become: A generic shell or unrestricted command runner
A safety-ceremony server that makes trusted local development slower than direct work
A prompt factory that optimizes for local technical tasks while forgetting the product and user
An enterprise workflow or approval platform
A hosted repository service or source-code exfiltration path
A replacement for Git, the implementation agent, or product judgment
experience_principles: Product or operational outcome before implementation detail
Autonomy with safety implemented mostly as server-side infrastructure
A small number of high-leverage tools over visible workflow ceremony
Repository truth and actual diff evidence over agent claims
Local-first operation with no automatic push or deployment
Technical precision when it represents a real contract, not habitual micromanagement
